routes.label: Prove the two equal-sine families from the unit circle, then count their union
Factor the sine difference and count the two zero families

changes.rationale: Equal unit-circle heights give x=2k*pi/(n-1) or x=(2k+1)*pi/(n+1), restricted to [0,pi]. Their cardinalities sum to n+1. An overlap can only be pi/2, and occurs iff n is 1 mod 4. Thus F(n)=n+1-1_{n=1 mod4}. Pairing 3 through 2008 gives 1003*2011=2017033, and exactly 501 indices 5,9,...,2005 require one subtraction. The factorization alternative follows from the explicit h070 identity and has the same complete counting step.

routes.label: Use right-triangle similarity, collinearity and algebraic elimination
Find the second circle intersection along AC and eliminate its scale

changes.rationale: The actual diagram fixes A=(0,0), O=(a,0), B=(2a,0), C above B. With r=AE=sqrt(x^2+y^2) and L=AC, collinearity gives L/r=2a/x. Right-triangle similarity gives AD*AC=4a^2. Thus AE=DC=L-4a^2/L. Eliminating L yields (2a-x)*y^2=x^3, with 0<x<2a,y>0 on the depicted nondegenerate branch. The circle-line scale method instead obtains AD=2ax/r from the second circle intersection and yields the same identity. Denominators and the selected branch are checked in both routes.

routes.label: Map the boundaries and prove sufficiency with nonnegative square roots
Interpret u+iv=(x+iy)^2 and use the first-quadrant square root with both coordinate bounds

changes.rationale: The coordinate edges map onto v=0,-1<=u<=1, and x=1,y=1 give u=1-v^2/4 and u=v^2/4-1. Necessity follows from (1-x^2)(1+y^2)>=0 and its swap. For sufficiency put R=sqrt(u^2+v^2), x=sqrt((R+u)/2), y=sqrt((R-u)/2). In the proposed cap v>=0 and v^2<=4(1-|u|), so R+|u|<=2; hence x,y are in [0,1] and map to (u,v). This proves the full filled image, not just its boundary, and matches actual choice D.

routes.label: Add signed lower bounds and check simultaneous equality
Compare affine slopes between all absolute-value breakpoints

changes.rationale: The integer sums are sum(1..84)=3570 and sum(85..119)=7140-3570=3570. By the absolute-value definition, |k*x-1|>=1-k*x for k<=84 and >=k*x-1 for k>=85. Adding gives f(x)>=84-35+x*(3570-3570)=49 for every real x. Equality holds exactly when all chosen signs agree, namely 1/85<=x<=1/84, including both endpoints. Hence 49 is an attained global minimum. Alternatively, on (1/(m+1),1/m) the piecewise-linear slope is 7140-m*(m+1). It is negative for m>=85, zero for m=84, and positive for m<=83; the outer unbounded intervals have slopes -7140 and +7140. This confirms the same entire minimum interval without differentiation.

routes.label: Locate the centers, compute area, and factor its difference from the maximum

changes.rationale: Put beta=angle CBA=60 degrees+t. Since AC>=AB and beta<=90 degrees, 0<=t<=30 degrees. Set B=(0,0), C=(1,0) with A above BC. The sine law gives circumradius 1/sqrt(3). Direct side-line, perpendicular-bisector, altitude and angle-bisector intersections give O=(1/2,1/(2sqrt(3))), H=(1/2-sin(2t)/sqrt(3),(cos(2t)-1/2)/sqrt(3)), I=(1/2-sin(t)/sqrt(3),(cos(t)-1/2)/sqrt(3)). The vertex chain B,C,O,I,H is simple in the open interval: H,I,O have increasing x and y coordinates, with the other edges on the right and bottom; the endpoints are its continuous degenerate limits. Shoelace and the sine-difference formula reduce the area to K=(sin(60 degrees-2t)+2sin(t))/6. Let s=t-20 degrees, so -20<=s<=10 degrees. The exact identity 6*(K-sin(20 degrees)/2)=2*(1-cos(s))*(sin(s-20 degrees)-2sin(20 degrees)) follows by expanding with h070, cofunction identities and the printed cosine double-angle formula. The first factor is nonnegative, while sin(s-20 degrees)<0 and sin(20 degrees)>0, so the other factor is strictly negative throughout. Equality occurs exactly at s=0 in this interval. Thus the unique maximum occurs at t=20 degrees and beta=80 degrees. This proves the bound and equality without sine concavity, Jensen or trigonometric differentiation.
